body.statement: For every integer \(K\geq2\), every real polynomial that uniformly approximates the signed Boolean OR function on \(\{\pm1\}^K\) with error at most \(1/14\) has total degree at least \(\sqrt K\).

source.verbatim_statement: The \(1/14\)-approximate degree of OR on \(n\) bits is at least \(\sqrt n\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:0803.4516v1, Theorem 7; the emitted node only renames the source's bit count from \(n\) to \(K\).

body.justification: This is the published approximate-degree lower bound used by the Boolean-slice reduction.
body.gap: The source supplies the Boolean degree obstruction, not the statistical reduction or a minimax theorem.
body.consumer: The proof of \(\mathrm{lem{:}or\text{-}obstruction}\) converts maximum approximation into the source's signed-OR convention.
